subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR6 a/b - the character-for-character replacement in both directions, realized for the first time by kb/Work PB793 (before it, every non-identity set was refused at compile time and GR6 had nothing to do). The correspondence is a COMPILE-TIME artifact of the named alphabet (12.3.7.4 GR7 i), emitted into the generated program as a 256-entry char[] literal exactly as a collating sequence's weights are, so the runtime holds no code page and knows no alphabet name. The boundary is the ONE physical transfer point of each organization and nowhere else - SequentialConnector.NextFrame on the read side, its EmitRecord / EmitRecordLine / OverwriteInPlace twins on the write side, and RecordFraming's store payload for RELATIVE and INDEXED - so a record area, a key value, a comparison and a lock identity are always in the native character set, which is what every other rule is written about. The golden proves both directions independently: the round trip restores AB012, and a second file description with no CODE-SET clause reads the same physical file as 194 195 241 242 243, the native ordinals of X'C1 C2 F0 F1 F2'.
